newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-VIMPANI CENTURY LEADS VICTORIA TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-VIMPANI CENTURY LEADS VICTORIA TO VICTORY.

text.p: Opener Graeme Vimpani hit a match-turning century on Sunday as Victoria scored an unlikely Sheffield Shield win over New South Wales.
Victoria, set 391 to win, reached their target for the loss of eight wickets to score a two-wicket victory after New South Wales had controlled the match for the first three days.
It was the highest winning total scored by Victoria in the final innings of a match since they hit 434 in 1932 to beat New South Wales, also at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

Vimpani resumed unbeaten on 77 with Victoria 136 without loss and went on to make 161, his highest score in first-class cricket. Victoria got their first scent of victory after a first-wicket partnership of 150 between Vimpani and Australia opener Matthew Elliott, who made 65.

Pace bowler Phil Alley claimed the wickets of both openers and Victoria later had a scare as medium-pace bowler Brad McNamara took three wickets in five balls to move them from 379 for five to 382 for eight.
Victoria captain Tony Dodemaide steadied the innings to steer his side to victory.
New South Wales, who led by 126 on the first innings, were not helped by an ankle injury suffered on Saturday by pace bowler Anthony Stuart.
In Brisbane, the match between Queensland and Shield leaders Western Australia petered out to a draw after more than four hours' play on the final day was lost to rain.
Queensland had been close to a win after reducing Western Australia to 96 for four on Saturday, leaving them needing another 313 for victory.
Western Australia captain Tom Moody saved his side from defeat with 136 as the visitors reached 273 for five before play was halted.
In Adelaide, opener Jamie Cox was denied a century but handed Tasmania a slight advantage by the close on the second day of the match against South Australia.

Tasmania reached 304 for six by the close in response to South Australia's first innings of 293. Cox fell to leg-spinner Peter McIntyre for 94 at the end of a 158-run partnership with fellow-opener Dene Hills. Hills was out to all-rounder Shane George for 59.
Western Australia lead the shield standings on 28 points, six clear of New South Wales.
